tests.description: Timed check on Semiotics and Staging Terminology

questions.question: Explain the difference between denotation and connotation, using a specific example from a production you have seen.
questions.correctAnswer: Denotation is the literal meaning; connotation is the associated meaning. E.g. a wedding dress denotes a bride's clothing but connotes purity, commitment, social expectation. Always link to specific production examples.

questions.question: How does a director use proxemics and levels to communicate the relationship between two characters?
questions.correctAnswer: Proxemics: close = intimacy or threat; far = distance or conflict. Levels: higher = power, authority; lower = vulnerability, submission. Give a specific scene example showing both working together.

questions.question: Describe how semiotics helps an audience understand the deeper meaning of a performance.
questions.correctAnswer: Semiotics reveals that every choice on stage is meaningful — costume, lighting, position, gesture all carry significance beyond their literal function. Analysing signs reveals the production's deeper themes.
